artists.biography:
At the Drive-In was an American post-hardcore band from El Paso, Texas, formed in 1993. Consisting of singer Cedric Bixler, guitarists Jim Ward and Omar Rodríguez, bassist Paul Hinojos, and drummer Tony Hajjar, the band released three studio albums and five EPs before breaking up in 2001. Their final album, 2000's Relationship of Command, received a number of accolades and is cited as a landmark of the post-hardcore genre.

Following the breakup, Bixler-Zavala and Rodríguez-López formed The Mars Volta while Ward, Hinojos, and Hajjar formed Sparta. At the Drive-In reunited in January 2012 and played the 2012 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, as well as the 2012 Lollapalooza Festival, but currently have no plans to perform or record any new material in the future.

Consisting of singer Cedric Bixler, guitarists Jim Ward and Omar Rodríguez, bassist Paul Hinojos, and drummer Tony Hajjar, the band released three studio albums and five EPs before breaking up in 2001. Their final album, 2000's Relationship of Command, received a number of accolades and is cited as a landmark of the post-hardcore genre.

Following the breakup, Bixler-Zavala and Rodríguez-López formed The Mars Volta while Ward, Hinojos, and Hajjar formed Sparta. At the Drive-In reunited in January 2012 and played the 2012 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, as well as the 2012 Lollapalooza Festival, but currently have no plans to perform or record any new material in the future.

perplexity.description:
in•ter a•li•a is the fourth and final studio album by American rock band At the Drive-In, released on May 5, 2017, through Rise Records. Marking their first full-length release of new material in 17 years since 2000’s acclaimed Relationship of Command, the album sees the band reuniting with guitarist Omar Rodríguez-López and producer Rich Costey. Musically, in•ter a•li•a blends the band’s signature post-hardcore intensity with progressive rock elements, angular guitar riffs, dynamic shifts, and impassioned vocals. The album’s sound is both a continuation of their earlier chaotic energy and a more refined, mature evolution, reflecting the members’ individual growth during their time apart.

The album’s lyrical themes touch on personal and societal issues, including trauma and empowerment, as exemplified by tracks like “Incurably Innocent,” which addresses sexual abuse. in•ter a•li•a received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its ambitious songwriting and emotional depth, though some noted it didn’t quite reach the groundbreaking heights of Relationship of Command. Commercially, the album performed modestly, debuting on several rock and alternative charts, and was supported by a major international tour. As At the Drive-In’s final studio release, in•ter a•li•a stands as a significant, if not definitive, chapter in their influential rock discography.
